analysis.title: Global Economics Daily Points, November 18, 2026
key_insights: Nvidia's earnings beat the evening before had very limited spillover into broader risk appetite. The Nasdaq outperformed, S&P futures saw lighter spillover, and equities elsewhere were on the back foot.

The dollar was somewhat firmer against several crosses, led by weakness in sterling, the euro, MXN and the rand. CAD was flat. North American sovereign yields were little changed. Gold fell sharply and oil was a few dimes lower.
The FOMC minutes for the October 27-28 meeting are described as stale before release (2pm ET) because a large amount of Fed-speak has already hit markets from all officials except the Chair.
Warm core CPI, a solid nonfarm payrolls report and Fed-speak have raised pricing for the December FOMC meeting from about 20bps to approaching 30bps of easing or tightening, as the report words it.

BoC Deputy Governor Gravelle speaks at 12:30pm ET on scenario analysis and the risk-management approach to monetary policy. There is no press conference. Scotiabank expects him to be more forward-looking than backward-looking on this week's CPI. Governor Macklem speaks next week, the last word before the pre-decision blackout.

PM Carney and Trump reportedly met for about 20 minutes on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen. Guidance was that they agreed to continue to work and stay in close contact. Carney has said progress is being made on a limited bilateral deal to lower tariffs, and that the viability of the auto sector is key.

UK CPI matched consensus at 3.6% y/y and services inflation stabilized, which caught positioning off guard. The 2-year gilt richened about 6bps, which the report calls a possible overreaction at the front end.

Chilean Q3 GDP fell 1.8% q/q SA against an expected -1.4%. Mining fell 12.9% on copper output down 11.9%. Agriculture and construction each fell 1.8%, financial services fell 1.1%, and manufacturing fell 0.5%.

Chile's central bank must weigh persistent upside CPI surprises (October at 4.5% y/y from 4.1%) against a weakening economy. Markets price about a four-in-ten chance of a hike on December 15 and about a full hike by the January 26 meeting.

Australian 2-year yields fell another 5bps overnight, extending the move that began after Monday's RBA minutes. Three dissenters in the minutes downplayed inflation upside risks and flagged downside risks to the economy and unemployment.

Australian Q3 wages rose 3.5% y/y and 1.1% q/q SA, a tenth above expectations, largely because Q2 was revised down to 0.7% from 0.8%. The annualized quarterly pace remains well above the RBA's 2-3% target range. October jobs data are due at 7:30pm ET. Employment has declined in two of the past three months and the unemployment rate is 4.7%.

Bank Indonesia hiked 25bps, siding with the minority of forecasters (16 of 38). The governor called it pre-emptive against inflation risk and rupiah weakness. The rupiah is down about 4% since September.

The rand was among the worst performers despite warmer South African core CPI, because gold fell about US$86 to about $3,760/oz. Gold is more than $1,600 below this year's peak and about $900 below late August. The SARB is widely expected to hold on November 19 while voicing concern about gold prices.
earnings_insights: Nvidia reported solid earnings the evening of November 17, which the report describes as a beat. No EPS or revenue figures are given.

risk_factors: Tech earnings strength is not lifting broader risk appetite, and equities outside the US are weak.
The gold plunge (down about $86 to about $3,760/oz) pressures gold-linked economies and currencies such as South Africa's rand.
The RBA minutes show three dissenters worried about a sharper downturn and rising unemployment, against wage growth that remains above the inflation target range.
Persistent upside inflation in Chile (CPI 4.5% y/y) against falling GDP leaves the central bank with a difficult trade-off.
Rupiah depreciation of about 4% since September is creating stability risks that Bank Indonesia cited for its hike.

vol_and_positioning: Positioning in gilts was caught off guard by UK CPI, which may have driven an overreaction toward lower front-end yields (2-year gilt richened about 6bps).

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish side: Q3 wages rose 3.5% y/y, and the annualized quarterly pace stays well above the RBA's 2-3% target range, which points to second-round inflation pressure.
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish side: three RBA dissenters flagged downside risks to the economy and unemployment, which has risen to 4.7%. Short-term yields fell on the minutes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: October Australian jobs data due 7:30pm ET on November 18. The report notes employment has fallen in two of the past three months.

theme_stances.key_argument: RBA minutes showed widening disagreement, with three dissenters pointing to downside risks and unemployment costs, which drove reduced hike bets.
theme_stances.evidence: widening disagreement on the state of the economy and forward-looking risks

theme_stances.key_argument: The plunge in gold outweighed warm South African core CPI in driving a weaker rand.
theme_stances.evidence: The culprit is probably the plunging price of gold
